# @ccm/ds

> CCM design-system Nuxt layer: Nuxt UI v4 + Utopia fluid tokens + Every Layout composition components + domain foundations.

Machine-readable source of truth: manifest.json (schema ccm-ds/manifest@1). This file is GENERATED from it by scripts/build-llms.mjs — do not edit by hand.

## Doctrine

- Pages compose components — a page file wires existing Nuxt UI and Ccm components together; it does not build widgets or layouts out of raw markup and utility soup.
- Class strings live only inside Tailwind Variants definitions (component files). Outside components/, class attributes are budgeted by lint (ccm/class-budget); pass props, not classes.
- Nuxt UI is restyled through app.config.ts (`ui` key) only — never inline :ui props, never scattered CSS overrides.
- ccm-layer CSS is plain CSS written on the design tokens (var(--spacing-*), var(--text-step-*), var(--color-*)) — no raw hex, no raw px (Stylelint enforces this).
- @apply is reserved for prose/markdown styling — never use it to build components.

## Components

### CcmStack

Every Layout Stack (ch. 01): injects block-start margins between stacked siblings via the owl selector — spacing belongs to the context, not the elements.

When to use: Vertical rhythm between any run of siblings: page sections, form fields, article flow. Reach for this instead of `flex flex-col gap-*` outside components/.

Props:
- `as` (string, default: "div") — Element (or component) to render.
- `space` (SpaceToken, default: "m") — Utopia space token between siblings.
- `recursive` (boolean, default: false) — Apply the spacing at any nesting depth, not only to direct children.
- `splitAfter` (number (1-5), no default) — Push everything after the nth child to the block-end edge (auto margin). Invalid values are ignored with a console warning.

Slots:
- `default` — The stacked children.

Anti-patterns:
- Adding vertical margins to the children — the Stack owns the spacing.
- Rebuilding it as `flex flex-col gap-*` in a page — compose CcmStack instead.
- splitAfter outside 1-5 — the CSS only enumerates five positions.

Source: app/components/CcmStack.vue

### CcmCluster

Every Layout Cluster (ch. 04): a wrapping flex row for groups of variable-length items spaced with gap.

When to use: Tag lists, button groups, nav links, metadata rows — anything that should wrap naturally when it runs out of inline space.

Props:
- `as` (string, default: "div") — Element (or component) to render.
- `space` (SpaceToken, default: "m") — Utopia space token for the gap.
- `justify` (string (CSS justify-content), default: "flex-start") — CSS justify-content value.
- `align` (string (CSS align-items), default: "flex-start") — CSS align-items value.

Slots:
- `default` — The clustered items.

Anti-patterns:
- Single-file horizontal scroll strips — that is CcmReel.
- Two-pane layouts that should switch orientation at a width — that is CcmSwitcher.

Source: app/components/CcmCluster.vue

### CcmGrid

Every Layout Grid (ch. 08): auto-filling column grid via `minmax(min(<min>, 100%), 1fr)` — container-intrinsic in pure CSS, single column below the minimum, no media queries.

When to use: Card grids and galleries where the column count should follow the container, not viewport breakpoints.

Props:
- `as` (string, default: "div") — Element (or component) to render.
- `min` (string (CSS length), default: "calc(var(--measure) / 3)") — Minimum column width; default set in CSS to a third of the measure.
- `space` (SpaceToken, default: "m") — Utopia space token for the gap.

Slots:
- `default` — The grid cells.

Anti-patterns:
- Fixed column counts (`grid-cols-3` + breakpoint variants) for content that should be container-intrinsic.
- Passing a token name as `min` — it takes a CSS length (e.g. '15rem'), not a SpaceToken.

Source: app/components/CcmGrid.vue

### CcmReel

Every Layout Reel (ch. 10): a single-file flex row that scrolls horizontally on overflow with native scrollbar affordance. No JavaScript.

When to use: Browsable strips — card rows, image rails, slidable link bars — where native continuous scrolling is the whole interaction.

Props:
- `as` (string, default: "div") — Element (or component) to render.
- `space` (SpaceToken, default: "s") — Utopia space token between items.
- `itemWidth` (string (CSS width), default: "auto") — Width for each item; 'auto' leaves items their intrinsic width.
- `height` (string (CSS block-size), default: "auto") — Block-size for the reel; 'auto' tracks the tallest item.
- `noBar` (boolean, default: false) — Hide the scrollbar (for a11y-neutral strips like link bars).

Slots:
- `default` — The reel items.

Anti-patterns:
- Paged sliding with dots/arrows/autoplay/snap points — that is Nuxt UI's UCarousel, not CcmReel.
- Adding JS scroll hijacking on top — native overflow scrolling is the contract.

Source: app/components/CcmReel.vue

### CcmSwitcher

Every Layout Switcher (ch. 06), implemented with container queries (PRO-229 deviation from the book's flex-basis hack). Switches between horizontal and vertical flex at a container-based breakpoint.

When to use: Rows that must stack when their CONTAINER (not the viewport) gets narrow: media-object pairs, action bars, side-by-side panels.

Props:
- `as` (string, default: "div") — Element (or component) to render.
- `threshold` ('xs' | 's' | 'm' | 'l' | 'xl', default: "s") — Named container breakpoint below which children stack (xs=20rem, s=30rem, m=40rem, l=50rem, xl=60rem). Enumerated because @container size conditions cannot read custom properties.
- `space` (SpaceToken, default: "m") — Utopia space token for the gap.
- `limit` (number (1-6), default: 4) — Quantity threshold: with more than this many children the layout stays vertical regardless of width.

Slots:
- `default` — The switching children.

Anti-patterns:
- Passing a free CSS length as threshold — only the xs–xl names exist.
- Viewport media queries for component-level layout switches — the whole point is container-based.

Source: app/components/CcmSwitcher.vue

### CcmCover

Every Layout Cover (ch. 07): a min-height column with one principal element vertically centered via auto block margins, optionally book-ended by header/footer children. Default min height 100svh.

When to use: Viewport-height heroes and cover screens: heading centered, optional bar above and call-to-action below.

Props:
- `as` (string, default: "div") — Element (or component) to render.
- `space` (SpaceToken, default: "m") — Utopia space token between/around children.
- `minHeight` (string (CSS min-block-size), default: "100svh") — Minimum block size of the cover.
- `noPad` (boolean, default: false) — Drop the padding on the container element.

Slots:
- `default` — Children; the centered one is the `h1` or any child carrying the `data-cover-centered` attribute.

Anti-patterns:
- Centering one box inside another — that is `grid place-items-center`, not a Cover.
- Forgetting the principal element: without an h1 or data-cover-centered child nothing centers.

Source: app/components/CcmCover.vue

### CcmFrame

Every Layout Frame (ch. 09): holds any child to a fixed aspect ratio; replaced children (img/video) fill and crop via object-fit, anything else is centered and clipped.

When to use: Media in cards and previews that must keep a fixed aspect ratio regardless of the source dimensions.

Props:
- `as` (string, default: "div") — Element (or component) to render.
- `ratio` (`${number}:${number}`, default: "16:9") — Aspect ratio as 'width:height', e.g. '16:9', '4:5', '1:1'. Typed because untyped ratios produced repeated 4:5 cover-crop bugs in Social House.
- `fit` ('cover' | 'contain', default: "cover") — How replaced children fill the frame: 'cover' crops, 'contain' letterboxes.

Slots:
- `default` — The framed child (usually an img or video).

Anti-patterns:
- Overriding object-fit in CSS instead of passing `fit`.
- Malformed ratios — anything not 'W:H' falls back to 16:9 with a console warning.

Source: app/components/CcmFrame.vue

### CcmChannelBadge

Brand-colored channel badge (icon + label) driven by the channel registry.

When to use: Labelling content with its social platform anywhere a compact branded chip fits.

Props:
- `channel` (string | null, no default) — Channel name, free-form (e.g. 'instagram', 'Twitter'); alias-aware, unknown values fall back to neutral.
- `label` (string, no default) — Optional label override (platform names are proper nouns — rarely needed).

Anti-patterns:
- Hardcoding platform hex colors — brand color comes from the channels registry, the sanctioned token exception.

Source: app/components/CcmChannelBadge.vue

### CcmChannelIcon

Channel id -> platform SVG mark (alias-aware; neutral globe fallback).

When to use: Rendering a platform mark on its own, without the badge chrome.

Props:
- `channel` (string | null, no default) — Channel name, free-form (e.g. 'instagram', 'Twitter').

Source: app/components/CcmChannelIcon.vue

### CcmStatusBadge

Status badge rendering the STATUS_COLORS mechanism via themed --ui-* variables.

When to use: Showing content workflow state (draft/pending/published/…) as a badge. The single status→color mechanism — never map status to color anywhere else.

Props:
- `status` (string | null, no default) — Status id, free-form ('published', 'In Buffer', 'draft'); normalized internally.
- `label` (string, no default) — Already-translated label override (takes precedence over `locale`).
- `locale` (string, default: "en") — Locale for the built-in dictionaries (en/pt).

Anti-patterns:
- Per-status CSS forks or ad-hoc status→color maps in consuming apps — STATUS_COLORS in app/utils/status.ts is the single source.

Source: app/components/CcmStatusBadge.vue

## Composables

### useClipboard

Composable wrapper over copyToClipboard preserving the `const { copy } = useClipboard()` call-site shape.

Source: app/composables/useClipboard.ts

## Utilities

### channels

Social-channel registry: {label, brandColor, fg, monochrome, icon} per platform (8: instagram, linkedin, x, facebook, youtube, tiktok, google_my_business, bluesky) + resolveChannel/channelBrand/channelIds. Sole home of brand hex (sanctioned token exception).

Anti-patterns:
- Hardcoding platform brand hex anywhere else — this file is the only sanctioned hex location.

Source: app/utils/channels.ts

### status

Status conventions: STATUS_COLORS map (status id -> semantic color: success/info/warning/error/neutral) as the single badge-coloring mechanism, plus EN/PT label dictionaries (STATUS_MESSAGES), statusColor/statusLabel/statusLabelKey/normalizeStatus/statusIds.

Source: app/utils/status.ts

### formatDate

Locale-aware, UTC-stable date formatter (Intl-based, no date-fns). formatDate(value, { locale, style }) — defensive: empty -> '', unparseable strings pass through.

Source: app/utils/format-date.ts

### copyToClipboard

Framework-agnostic clipboard write: navigator.clipboard with hidden-textarea/execCommand fallback. Never throws; resolves boolean.

Source: app/utils/clipboard.ts

### composition

Shared prop types/guards for the composition components: SPACE_TOKENS (the 9 Utopia steps + 8 one-step pairs), spaceVar(), SWITCHER_THRESHOLDS (xs=20rem…xl=60rem), FrameRatio parsing. SpaceToken values: 3xs 2xs xs s m l xl 2xl 3xl 3xs-2xs 2xs-xs xs-s s-m m-l l-xl xl-2xl 2xl-3xl.

Source: app/utils/composition.ts

## Deliberately not shipped (do not reintroduce)

Every Layout primitives (and near relatives) the layer intentionally omits:

- **Icon** — Every Layout's Icon layout (icon-to-text sizing/alignment) is deliberately not shipped. Use instead: UIcon (Nuxt UI + Iconify) for general icons; the layer only ships brand marks via CcmChannelIcon.
- **Imposter** — Every Layout's Imposter (positioned overlay) is deliberately not shipped — overlays are widget territory: focus traps, dismissal, ARIA. Use instead: UModal for dialogs, UPopover for anchored overlays.
- **Box** — Every Layout's Box (padded/bordered container) is deliberately not shipped — a component wrapper adds nothing over one or two token-backed utilities. Use instead: Utility classes on the design tokens (e.g. p-s, border, rounded-sm) or UCard when it is card-shaped.
- **Center** — Every Layout's Center (measured horizontal centering with gutters) is deliberately not shipped. Use instead: UContainer for page-width centering; `mx-auto max-w-*` or `grid place-items-center` for one-off intrinsic centering.
- **Container** — No bespoke width-container component. Component-responsive behavior belongs to container queries, not wrapper components. Use instead: UContainer for the page shell; CSS container queries (the CcmSwitcher pattern) when a component must respond to its own width.
- **Sidebar** — Every Layout's Sidebar (sidebar-with-content pair) is deferred, not rejected — no consuming product needs it yet. Use instead: CcmSwitcher or a grid for now; when a sidebar pattern recurs (2+ real uses across consuming apps), extract it into the layer as CcmSidebar per the extraction rule.
